ends.start: N: ~1 channel-width past the north mouth at Point Defiance, stopping short of the Dalco Passage / East Passage junction (the 150 m East Passage basin takes over at 47.310)
ends.end: S: the south mouth at Point Fosdick, stopping before the Hale Passage junction where the channel opens into the 3.5 km Fox Island basin (47.254 and south)

notes.flood_direction: Flood sets SOUTH through The Narrows (Admiralty Inlet -> South Sound). anchor.flood_deg 208.5 is PUG1527's floodDirection in Slackwater/Resources/currents.json; NOAA CO-OPS reports meanFloodDir 198 for bin 19 of the same station. The seed is therefore drawn N->S. The task brief's claim that flood sets N at Tacoma is wrong.
notes.spring_max_kn: max |Velocity_Major| = 6.58 kn at 2026-05-17 22:48Z, from CO-OPS currents_predictions interval=6 over the spring week 2026-05-14..2026-05-21 (new moon 2026-05-16). This is also the 2026 annual maximum for the station (MAX_SLACK scan of the full year).
notes.cd_to_mwl_m: MSL - MLLW at NOAA 9446484 Tacoma (Commencement Bay) = 7.46 - 0.62 ft = 6.84 ft = 2.085 m. Cross-check: 9446545 TACOMA 6.88 ft (2.097 m); 9446491 ARLETTA 7.60 ft (2.317 m) is the outlier and is on the Hale Passage side.
notes.max_half_width_m: 1400, not the 1100 first chosen. 1100 was picked to cap the degenerate cross-channel sections that the unconstrained thalweg refinement produced; with the refinement now slew-limited those are gone, and 1100 was clipping the real north-mouth sections by ~10% (2180 m of channel read as 1970 m at PUG1524). At 1400 every width is bounded by land, not by the window: the widths at half-width 1600 and 2200 are identical to those at 1400.
notes.check_stations: PUG1524 and PUG1526 sit at the north mouth (sections 2-3, widths 2180/2090 m) — outside the flare-terminated kept_range [18, 46] (spec 3, limit 1.3 x 1370 = 1781 m). They are recorded here as reference_stations, not graded: their first-run numbers (CERTIFICATION.md) are the empirical case for the bounds rule, not a verdict on the in-bounds patch. PUG1528 (section 43) is the in-bounds check; the reciprocal_check grades PUG1527 from a PUG1528 anchor over the same geometry.
notes.bathymetry: NOAA Office of Coast Survey National Bathymetric Source. BlueTopo has NO Pacific Northwest coverage in the noaa-ocs-nationalbathymetry-pds bucket (verified: zero delivered tiles north of 42 N in UTM 10), so the 4 m NOAA Navigation Test-and-Evaluation BAG surfaces from the same bucket and the same NBS programme are used instead. Same vertical datum (MLLW), same elevation-up sign convention. See data/tiles/tacoma-narrows/MANIFEST.json.
